page: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is a shared-core virtual machine instance belonging to the e2 family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical Intel Xeon core with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is provisioned with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and is allocated zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the shared-core CPU allocation model limits multi-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is rated as average, scoring 2642.19, whereas the multi-core score of 2642.78 falls into the weak category. Memory performance is constrained, with read-only small block bandwidth at 39.35 GB/sec and uncached large block read bandwidth at 6.36 GB/sec, both categorized as poor. Geekbench scores reflect these limitations, with a single-core score of 661.0 and a multi-core score of 682.0. Static web serving throughput is measured at 0.63 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-medium offers a budget-friendly entry point for workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance compute resources. The shared-core architecture introduces performance tradeoffs, particularly under sustained multi-threaded loads, making it unsuitable for high-throughput databases or intensive data processing. It is best suited for low-traffic web serving, software development and testing environments, lightweight microservices, and basic background automation tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is a shared-core virtual machine instance designed for budget-conscious, low-intensity workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.2 GHz, it provides 2 vCPUs backed by a single physical core with hyper-threading, alongside 4.0 GB of system memory. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show average single-core capabilities with a stress-ng score of 2642.19, but weak multi-core and memory bandwidth results, reflecting its shared-resource architecture. Memory read-only large block bandwidth is limited to 6.36 GB/sec. This resource profile makes the e2-medium highly cost-efficient for development, testing, and low-traffic web serving, though it presents clear performance tradeoffs for sustained or memory-intensive applications.
